title: Broad bean and lentil fritters with minty yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Lentils, broad beans, feta, eggs, flour, yoghurt and salad leaves are all plain home staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Everything is a mainstream supermarket item at an everyday price, and broad beans in pods are on shelves in late May.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a frying pan and a bowl, and the techniques are within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: About 200g of skinned beans bound with 150g of cooked lentils, two eggs, flour and feta gives a soft but workable fritter mix for four, with a yoghurt dip and leaves.

honest_times.reason: 45 minutes of prep honestly covers double-podding 1kg of beans, chopping and frying in batches, and the 20 minutes of cook time matches the lentil simmer and bean boil.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, nothing unlisted appears apart from water, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fresh broad beans with mint suit a late-May lunch, and the beans are the bulk and point of the fritters.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, plain British English that a neighbour would follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Beans, lentils, eggs and feta with salad and yoghurt make a filling, protein-rich lunch a family would want again.
